title: DM Rush: Influencer Edition

selected_top_5_categories.reasoning: The playfield is split into left and right decision zones, and the player makes urgent binary choices against approaching targets in an endless arcade loop. It lacks literal lane switching movement, but the mechanical feel is the closest match in the category list.

The game relies on repeated rapid taps/clicks to process targets and accumulate score, with simple direct input and immediate reward/punishment feedback. It is more reflex-classification than idle clicking, so this is a secondary rather than primary match.

The fiction, UI language, and scoring frame the game around maintaining an influencer stream and audience approval. However, there are no management, upgrade, or economy layers typical of tycoon design, so the match is thematic more than systemic.

The title, message content, fan-count score, and stream-shutdown framing strongly support an influencer-themed simulation wrapper. The underlying mechanics are still arcade reflex play rather than broad life or social simulation.

The game is endless, escalates in speed, and asks the player to survive under increasing pressure. The fit is weakened because there is no avatar moving through space, but the escalating endless survival cadence is comparable.

uncertainty_notes: The category universe does not contain a perfect match for 'binary classification arcade game' or 'moderation reflex game,' so the best-fit categories are approximate.
Several high-ranking categories are chosen partly for interaction structure and partly for theme, because the game blends arcade mechanics with influencer-stream framing.
If the taxonomy favored pure mechanics over presentation, Lane runner game and Clicker game would dominate more clearly than the streamer/influencer labels.
